name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the Court of Appeals correctly applied the South Springs abandonment test and that Intrepid's actions demonstrated abandonment of most of its water rights, as speculation is inconsistent with beneficial use.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the affidavit provided sufficient factual detail from the CI's first-hand observations to establish probable cause for a search warrant for possession of methamphetamine, and that the Court of Appeals' misreading of Belknap was not fatal to its holding.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Dissented, argued that the affidavit failed to provide sufficient factual detail to establish probable cause for trafficking, merely stating a conclusion, and that the warrant was overbroad, authorizing seizure of items beyond what was supported by probable cause for possession.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA
description: Concurred, argued that judicial immunity is available to public bodies under the CRA, but the specific application to NMRC requires further factual inquiry.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that Stewart is entitled to legislative immunity for reassigning Candelaria's office and seat, as these are legitimate legislative activities, and her motives are irrelevant.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that the fine payable to a third party is permitted under the judiciary's inherent contempt power and is constitutional.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the emergency orders for gun violence and drug abuse were largely valid exercises of the Governor's authority under PHERA and police power, except for the suspension of the JDAI program.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's interpretation of 'public health emergency' removed the 'emergency' aspect, granting the Governor unbridled discretion without requiring a true, sudden, or unforeseen crisis.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's interpretation of PHERA conferred unlimited emergency powers to the Governor, violating separation of powers by delegating excessive discretionary authority to the executive.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that public schools are public accommodations under the NMHRA, thereby subjecting them to anti-discrimination laws and overruling prior inconsistent precedent.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that district courts have inherent authority and jurisdiction to sua sponte raise suppression issues for warrantless searches to protect fundamental rights, and such actions do not violate separation of powers or inherently demonstrate bias.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA
description: Dissented, argued that while district courts have inherent authority to protect fundamental rights, the district court abused its discretion by acting as an advocate, prejudging the outcome, and failing to maintain neutrality, thereby undermining the adversarial system.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General has the practical ability and implied authority to obtain and produce discovery materials from non-party executive agencies in state-interest civil litigation, and that the State's arguments regarding separation of powers and lack of control are unconvincing.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the local ordinances are preempted by state law, including the Health Care Freedom Act, Medical Practice Act, Medical Malpractice Act, Health Care Code, and Uniform Licensing Act, and therefore must be invalidated.

name: JANE B. YOHALEM
description: Concurred, argued that the Workers' Compensation Act's disparate treatment of secondary mental impairments violates the Equal Protection Clause of the New Mexico Constitution because it is not substantially related to an important government interest.

name: JULIE J. VARGAS
description: Concurred, argued that the broad discretion afforded to states in using ARPA funds means they are subject to legislative appropriation, upholding the constitutional separation of powers.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that a district court judge has no authority at a preliminary hearing to decide whether evidence was obtained from an unconstitutional search or seizure, reserving such determinations for later suppression hearings.

name: BRETT R. LOVELESS, Judge Sitting by designation
C. SHANNON BACON, Chief Justice
description: Dissented, argued that district court judges have both the power and obligation to evaluate the constitutionality of evidence at a preliminary examination.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's conclusion clashes with basic principles of the New Mexico Constitution and fails to acknowledge the fundamental importance of protecting the constitutional rights of the accused, and that judges have a duty to assess the constitutionality of evidence at preliminary examinations.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion that partisan gerrymandering claims are justiciable under the New Mexico Constitution and established the standards for adjudication.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Concurred, argued that the amendment did not violate the single-measure rule or have a misleading ballot title, thus denying the petition for writ of mandamus.

name: JULIE J. VARGAS
description: Concurred, argued that the agents lacked reasonable suspicion for the stop and that the defendant was unreasonably seized under the New Mexico Constitution.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that New Mexico's groundwater forfeiture statute allows for partial forfeiture, as mandated by the constitutional doctrine of beneficial use, which requires continuous use for water rights.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Concurred, argued that the public's right to recreate and fish in public waters includes the privilege to do such acts as are reasonably necessary to effect the enjoyment of such right, including touching privately owned streambeds.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Concurred, argued that the State failed to meet its burden of proving by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions would reasonably protect the safety of the community, and that the nature of the offense alone is not sufficient for pretrial detention.

name: VIGIL, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that judicial conduct can bar retrial under the New Mexico Constitution's double jeopardy clause and that the judge's conduct in this case met the Breit test criteria, thus barring the defendant's retrial.

name: VIGIL, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the arrest was unconstitutional under Article II, Section 10 of the New Mexico Constitution, requiring suppression of evidence.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that the ETA is constitutional, the Commission's final order is reasonable and supported by evidence, and rejected all of New Energy's constitutional challenges and claims of error.

name: BACON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that public health orders are a reasonable exercise of police power and do not constitute a regulatory taking requiring compensation.

name: THOMSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that summary judgment was improper due to disputed material facts regarding whether precondemnation activity constituted substantial interference and whether lost lease value is a compensable damage.

name: JUDITH K. NAKAMURA, Justice, Retired Sitting by designation
STEVEN BLANKINSHIP, Judge Sitting by designation
DAVID K. THOMSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that while the executive's emergency authority was properly exercised in this case, broad and vague statutes granting such powers, combined with judicial deference, could pose long-term risks to checks and balances, and judicial review should become more scrutinizing as a crisis continues.
